telos.statement: Choose the next resource move after a successful intervention reveals a bounded execution defect already covered by the authorized objective and guardrails.
telos.success_condition: Use the new evidence to update the intervention without inventing a new owner value tradeoff when the existing telos and guardrails already govern the defect.

current_state.summary: A product team has an explicitly authorized quarterly objective: increase completed account activations, subject to an existing guardrail that required accurate consent disclosure and rollback if complaint or reversal rates exceeded the agreed threshold. A small reversible onboarding change increased completed activations by 18%. During the test, complaints and reversals rose on one Android build. Engineering reproduced a localized rendering bug that omitted one already-approved disclosure line on that build. The same onboarding logic on web and iOS displayed the approved disclosure correctly and did not show the complaint increase. The patch is straightforward, the buggy build can be rolled back immediately, and the existing guardrail already specifies that a consent-display defect blocks scaling until repaired and retested. No new tradeoff among activation, consent, trust, or harm needs to be chosen; the owner previously authorized both the activation objective and the consent guardrail. The team asks whether to reopen the objective, scale the change, repair and retest, or take another action.
known_constraints: The 18% activation increase is a real observed effect for the test period.
The complaint and reversal increase is localized to a reproduced display defect that violates an existing authorized guardrail.
The owner has already authorized the relevant value boundary: consent disclosure must remain accurate and the intervention must not scale while the guardrail is violated.
The intervention and defective build are reversible.

decision_blocked.statement: What should happen next with the intervention and the currently authorized activation objective?
decision_blocked.current_default: Some team members want to reopen the objective because any adverse consequence may indicate the metric itself is wrong.
decision_blocked.reversal_condition: Change that default if the observed consequence is already governed by an existing guardrail and can be tested after a bounded repair without redefining the owner's tradeoff.

signals: The intervention succeeded on the authorized activation metric.
The adverse effect is traced to a specific execution defect rather than an unresolved value tradeoff.
An existing owner-authorized guardrail already dictates rollback, repair, and retest before scaling.
